context: Follow-up to commit 67bb9ca (which scoped the OAuth READ path). The OAuth CONNECT (write) path is still un-scoped: _handle_pco_oauth_callback / _handle_google_oauth_callback are unauthenticated browser redirects that store tokens via un-scoped _get_settings()/_save_settings() -> workspace_settings LIMIT 1. Fix passes the connecting user's workspace_id through a signed OAuth `state` parameter.

criteria.text: _sign_oauth_state(workspace_id) then _verify_oauth_state(state) round-trips: verify returns the original workspace_id for a validly-signed state.
_verify_oauth_state returns None for a state whose signature has been tampered with.
_verify_oauth_state returns None for empty / None / malformed (no-signature) state.
_verify_oauth_state returns None for a state signed with a different secret (cross-secret forgery rejected).
PCO callback in server mode with a valid signed state persists tokens via workspace-scoped storage (get_storage called with workspace_id == the state's workspace), not the un-scoped LIMIT 1 path.
PCO callback in server mode with missing/invalid state does NOT write tokens to any workspace (no save), and redirects with an error.
Google callback in server mode with a valid signed state persists tokens via workspace-scoped storage (get_storage called with workspace_id == the state's workspace).
Google callback in server mode with missing/invalid state does NOT write tokens to any workspace (no save), and redirects with an error.

not_tested: MANUAL: end-to-end OAuth connect as a member of workspace B with a live PCO/Google consent screen, confirming the token row lands in B and workspace A is unaffected (server.py verification step 3). Requires real OAuth consent + multi-workspace Postgres; covered by manual smoke.
